author: Al Jazeera English
description:
A powerful 7.2-magnitude earthquake has struck southern Panama, prompting evacuations from buildings. The quake centred near Pitaloza Arriba in the central province of Herrera, at a depth of around 12 kilometres.

Al Jazeera’s Alessandro Rampietti says authorities are still assessing the damage, especially in the central and southern provinces closer to the epicentre, which was in a mostly rural area. A few buildings have been confirmed collapsed in the provinces of Herrera and Los Santos. Images show a collapsed hotel and the bell tower of a 16th-century church in the city of Atalaya.

So far, no casualties have been confirmed by the authorities. Rescue teams are still moving towards affected locations.

Al Jazeera’s Alessandro Rampietti reports from Bogota.

The International Criminal Court in The Hague has strongly rejected new US sanctions announced by the Trump administration and vowed to continue its work.

The court is the only permanent court prosecuting the worst crimes and is supported by 125 states. ICC President Tomoko Akane called the sanctions “an attack against sovereign states that have created the court” and “an attack against victims of mass atrocities”. She added: “The ICC will not bow to external threats.”

Al Jazeera’s Step Vaessen says the court has tried to become independent from US companies. But with European banks and other companies also complying with the sanctions, the ICC will face a real challenge in keeping operating.

The sanctions come hours after the Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the Nobel Peace Prize to former ICC judge Navi Pillay for her efforts to fight for international justice. 

The sanctions take effect in six months, giving European governments time to decide how to respond.

description:
The Labour Party has won a London parliamentary by-election, where Prime Minister Andy Burnham faced a crucial political test.

Sagal Abdi-Wali has been elected Member of Parliament for Holborn and St Pancras, a seat previously held by Burnham’s predecessor, Keir Starmer, whom the ruling Labour Party forced out as leader after poor local election results. 

Abdi-Wali leads the local council and is a familiar face in local politics. In her victory speech, she thanked voters, whether or not they backed her, and said: “This is Camden, and this is Britain.”

Al Jazeera’s Sonia Gallego, reporting live from the count, says the constituency is far from typical. 

Gallego says Labour feels “a deep sigh of relief”, though caution is needed. Voters want the government to tackle housing and the cost of living, and whether the so-called “Burnham bounce” carries nationally will depend on that.

Al Jazeera’s Sonia Gallego reports from central London.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has visited Berlin to meet German Chancellor Friedrich Merz at the Chancellery.

The official purpose of the visit was to ratify a defence co-operation protocol agreed between Merz and Burnham’s predecessor, Keir Starmer. But the visit also centred on the relationship between Burnham and Merz, and between the UK and the European Union.

Burnham has already said he wants a much closer, deeper relationship with the EU, and he pointed to a new summit coming up at the end of this year. 

In Merz, Burnham has a colleague who shares the idea of a much closer UK-EU relationship, and Merz’s Christian Democrats are willing to open the doors to the UK. But returning to the EU will not be easy. The French government welcomes the idea of the UK coming back, but not under the conditions that existed before Brexit.

Al Jazeera’s Dominic Kane reports from Berlin.

description:
Student protesters called for another day of mobilisation across France, including in the northern city of Lille, as high school students and supporters kept up pressure on the government.

The government has tried to show it is listening by opening a portal for students to submit complaints. Students have raised concerns about classroom conditions, including overcrowding.

But the French government has also stressed how difficult its budgetary situation is. France has a public debt problem, with a deficit of almost 5.5 percent, well above the European Union’s fiscal responsibility limit of around 3 percent. 

That response does not appear to have convinced protesters in Lille or elsewhere in the country. They say they will keep showing up and point to another nationwide day of mobilisation next week.

Al Jazeera’s Rosie Birchard reports from Lille.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Canadian writer Anne Carson has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature. The announcement was made in Stockholm on Thursday, a day before the Peace Prize in Oslo. Carson described the moment as “a little insane”, saying she was not expecting the accolade.

Carson, born in Toronto, is the 123rd laureate since the honour was inaugurated by Alfred Nobel’s will. 

The Swedish Academy commended her for translating and reworking classic Greek and Latin tales for a modern audience, including works such as “Autobiography of Red”. Nobel Committee member Steve Sem-Sandberg said her writing connects contemporary readers, used to screens and modern problems, with the literature of antiquity.

She is the 30th winner to write in English, and only a handful of laureates have written in non-European, non-Western languages. 

The prize carries $1.2 million in cash, and the fame can be life- and career-changing, turning winners into rock stars.

Al Jazeera’s Paul Rhys reports from Stockholm.

description:
Argentina’s government under President Javier Milei has launched international arbitration against Britain over the Sea Lion oil project, and says it will ask the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea to order a halt if Britain refuses to stop it. 

The move escalates a sovereignty dispute over the Falkland Islands, known in Argentina as the Malvinas, that has lasted nearly two centuries.

The Sea Lion field, around 220 kilometres north of the islands, sits above an estimated 1.7 billion barrels of oil. Israeli-listed Navitas Petroleum and the UK’s Rockhopper Exploration are jointly developing it. 

Argentina and Britain fought a war over the islands in 1982, which Britain won, but Buenos Aires never abandoned its claim. Milei also sees a possible opening in Washington, where Donald Trump has raised the possibility of reviewing the US position.
